kai: Quick note — observed SSE streams where a keepalive (empty data event) sent as CRLF (`data:\r\n\r\n`) sometimes merges with the following `data:` when the client reconnects. Parser in node sample-app chokes.

reena: Which node-sdk/sample versions?

kai: node-sdk v0.10.0, sample-app v1.5.2. Happens in CI linux runner and locally on mac. Browser SDK hasn't reproduced yet.

kai: Minimal repro: stream long response, interrupt TCP (vpn toggle), reconnect. Sometimes the reconstructed `data:` block contains an embedded `\r` or `\n` literal inside JSON, causing `JSON.parse` to fail. Example raw capture:

```:
data: {"msg":"first"}\r\n\r\ndata: {"msg":"second"}\r\n\r\n
```

kai: After reassembly client got `\{"msg\":\"first\"\}\r\n\{"msg\":\"second\"\}` as one data payload.

fernando: Likely `.split('\n\n')` + `.join('')` issue in sample parser — CRLF vs LF differences can leave stray `\r` chars.

reena: Patch idea: normalize CRLF to LF upfront, preserve `\n` when joining multiple `data:` lines (`join('\n')`), and treat whitespace-only data as heartbeat. Also add unit tests that split inside the sequence `data:\r` vs `\n` boundaries.

kai: Local quick fix I used:
```
buf = buf.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
const events = buf.split('\n\n');
const data = events...map(l => l.slice(5)).join('\n');
```
Reduced failures locally.

fernando: Good. Let's add a canonical `parseEventStream` util in node-sdk, update sample-app to import it, and add parity tests against python/browser.

ci-bot: CI queued for kai/sse-crlf-normalize (tests: sdk-stream-matrix).

reena: Actions: kai file GH issue + small PR with tests; fernando add util; add regression in sdk-stream-matrix fuzzer.

kai: Opening issue now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/issues/600 (WIP). Will attach tcpdump and failing logs.
